# CANDIDATE: TRENDLINE_BREAK_PUT_VETO

**Filed:** 2026-08-20
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** filter_change
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

We propose to add a symmetrical PUT veto using the same logic as the existing TRENDLINE_BREAK_CALL_VETO but inverted: block PUT entries when a confirmed bullish structure break is detected (i.e., a 5m close through a respected descending resistance level). This aims to prevent bearish entries during bullish momentum, thereby avoiding losses on PUT trades that go against the short-term trend.

## Mechanism

The veto will trigger when the market structure classifier (via `market_structure.py`) detects a bullish break of structure (BOS) or change of character (CHoCH) on the 5-minute timeframe, specifically a close above a previously respected descending trendline (or swing high) that had acted as resistance. When this condition is met, any PUT entry signal (from BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON or other setups) will be vetoed for the remainder of the day or until the structure is invalidated. The exit logic remains unchanged; this is purely an entry filter.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+; $1K paper ~= 14% headline (based on 3-contract minimum at $1K account).
2. **Sample bias:** We have not yet run any backtest for this candidate. The sample bias disclosure is pending OOS A/B. High overfit risk if not validated on out-of-sample data.
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (we plan to run OOS A/B on 2025-01-02..2026-06-18 real-fills curve as per task).
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (we have not yet validated on real fills for the top 3 J days).
5. **Failure modes:** 
   - Worst day: May inadvertently block PUT entries on days that turn out to be strong bearish days (e.g., 4/29, 5/01, 5/04), turning winners into losers.
   - Max drawdown: Could increase if we block winning PUT trades and the engine takes losses instead.
   - Blow-up scenario: If the veto triggers too frequently in choppy markets, it may cause the engine to miss opportunities and increase losing trades due to forced inactivity or taking suboptimal signals.
6. **Concentration:** unknown -- requires Stage-1 backtest (we cannot estimate concentration without backtest results).

Gym validators: 97/98 PASS, guard test: 7/7 PASS, walk-forward OOS positive with WF >= 0.70, real-fills validation on top 3 J days (diff < ±20%), anchor no-regression (edge_capture >= 771).

## Confidence

2 / 10 -- We have no data yet; this is a pure proposal based on inverting an existing gate that has not been proven effective as a discriminating PUT gate (as noted in WS4: "Does NOT fire as discriminating PUT gate (all 6 dates get breaks)"). We are inverting it to be a PUT veto, but we have no reason to believe it will be more effective.

## Pre-existing leaderboard impact

This candidate complements the existing TRENDLINE_BREAK_CALL_VETO (WS4) by adding the symmetrical PUT side. It may conflict with the STRUCTURE_VETO_DIR_VS_TREND (★) which already does a bidirectional veto (PUT in uptrend, CALL in downtrend). However, our veto is based on trendline breaks (via market_structure.py) while the STRUCTURE_VETO uses a different trend classification (classify_trend). They may be complementary or redundant; further study is needed.
